purpose: Deployment simulation asked by the user: enrol 15 of the 20 Train identities, then present the evaluation blocks of ALL 20 identities (15 enrolled + 5 unregistered) at once. Enrolled rows should be identified correctly, unregistered rows should be rejected (label 0). Reports overall correctness, identification accuracy, rejection rate, unregistered false-accept rate and a per-identity breakdown. Train-only simulation: no Test data are read, no Session field is used for any decision, no model is trained.

protocol.stage1_training: per-task mean/sd and the PCA basis are fitted on the fit rows (frac <= 0.6) of ALL 20 identities. Fold-invariant, computed once. This is the user-defined training stage; it is deliberately NOT restricted to the enrolled identities.
protocol.stage2_enrolment: prototypes of the 15 enrolled identities only, from their own prototype rows: variant 'fit' = fit rows (frac <= 0.6), variant 'fit_eval' = fit + eval rows (frac <= 0.8, upper-bound reference). k_proto = 12 for e65, 1 for subwin6 and e162.
protocol.stage3_deployment: every evaluation-block row (0.6 < frac <= 0.8) of ALL 20 identities is scored against the 15 enrolled prototypes: argmax over the enrolled identities = identification, best-match score < tau = rejection (label 0).
protocol.threshold_rule: tau = quantile(the 15 enrolled identities' best-match scores in the evaluation window, 1 - a); calibrated on enrolled identities only, the 5 unregistered never enter the threshold
protocol.fold_rule: k = 5: 500 distinct random 5-subsets of the 20 identities drawn from C(20,5) with numpy default_rng(20261116 + 5), i.e. the same generator and seed rule as E197 (E197 drew 200)

gates.name: subwin6_pca96_k1
gates.note: gate used by the E191 7/11 scheme

fusion_normalisation: Each stream's (rows x 20) identity-score matrix is standardised with the mean/sd of that fold's enrolled-known best-match scores (the max over the 15 enrolled columns), then the weighted sum is taken and the argmax is restricted to the enrolled columns. Single-stream gates are invariant to this step.

reporting.identification_accuracy: share of the enrolled 15 identities' evaluation rows whose argmax over the enrolled prototypes is their own identity (threshold-free)
reporting.rejection_rate: share of the 5 unregistered identities' evaluation rows whose best-match score is below tau (label 0)
reporting.false_accept_rate: share of the 5 unregistered identities' evaluation rows whose best-match score is >= tau and is therefore assigned to some enrolled identity
reporting.false_reject_rate: share of the enrolled identities' evaluation rows whose best-match score is below tau (an enrolled person is locked out)
reporting.overall_accuracy: (enrolled rows correctly identified + unregistered rows correctly rejected) / all 2301 evaluation rows - the task's definition; acceptance is not required for an enrolled row to count as identified
reporting.overall_end_to_end: (enrolled rows correctly identified AND accepted + unregistered rows rejected) / all rows - the stricter deployment reading that also pays the false-reject cost
reporting.closed_set_f1: macro-F1 of the argmax assignment over the 15 enrolled identities
reporting.auc: enrolled-known vs unregistered best-match scores, pooled over the 500 folds
reporting.test_official: N/A - this experiment is Train-only and does not read Test; AUC / F1 / C / RA / ASafeR / U / Score are not computed

references.test_s1_note: the task's 0.7415 equals E197's k=5 fold-matched Test S1 rejection averaged over its 9 unsupervised gates (results.json analysis.test_s1_match['5'].test_mean). It is a cross-batch reading and is quoted, not re-computed here
